races.paceDynamic: Silky Robin is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner sprint and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good to Firm ground at Brighton. The remainder of the field — Desdemona, Recon Mission, Harry Brown, and Marra Donna — are all natural hold-up horses, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly honest, which sets up a race that could easily become a procession for the leader if the gallop is measured. This field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate; Recon Mission and Harry Brown are genuine closers redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning they are unlikely to secure their preferred rearward position and may find themselves closer than ideal without that being their natural rhythm. The shape strongly favours Silky Robin front-running to a comfortable lead, making this a race where prominent and lead-from-the-front profiles have a significant structural advantage over true hold-up horses.

Every runner in the field is a hold-up or midfield type at best, so the contest will lack structure — expect a slow, processional first mile before the pace suddenly lifts late. The entirely hold-up profile of this field means that finishing speed, good ground handling, and the ability to quicken from a close-range position will be the decisive factors. This shape strongly favours horses who can travel economically in a compact group and produce a sharp turn of foot in the final two furlongs on good-to-firm ground. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Gearing's Point, Fighting Poet, Foinix, Sweetstevie, Dream Of Ithaca, and Highland Harvey are all genuine hold-up horses shown in midfield simply because there is no room for them all at the back, and none of them is likely to secure a truly natural position in the tactical, compressed shape this race will produce.

With every runner carrying a hold-up profile, the premium falls on late finishing speed and position off the home turn — horses who can hold a prominent enough berth when the tempo finally lifts will have a decisive edge over those trapped deepest in a six-runner field where there is little room to be buried. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — D Day Major Winter, Dash Of Class, Dora Vita, and Diamond Aura are all natural closers redistributed into midfield slots; of these, D Day Major Winter and Dash Of Class are most likely to secure a more prominent position given jockey intent and recent form trends. This race shape favours the runner who can travel mid-to-prominent, avoiding the drift-and-sprint trap, with a quick turn of foot when the race ignites — a tactically versatile, prominent-tracking profile holds the clearest edge.

watchPoints.text: Havana Mojito's price could shorten dramatically if it jumps cleanly and Luke Morris takes a clear lead — monitor the early exchanges closely because if it is pressured even slightly the entire race shape changes.

Dion Baker is the hold-up horse with the most credible finishing form but Darragh Keenan will need a gap to open in the straight; if the prominent group bunches on the rail, Baker's run could be blocked entirely.

Oh So Audacious and Aim For The Bull are both prominent types who will want the same ground tracking Havana Mojito — if they bump or jostle for position in the first two furlongs, one or both could lose their rhythm and their chance.

The redistribution of Henry Tudor, Daley T, Maury, and Bated Breeze into midfield means the back of the field will be unusually crowded with horses that are not natural finishers from deep — watch for traffic problems in the closing stages if the field fans wide.

Bear To Dream returns from 34 days off for Michael Attwater, who has had only one winner from 15 runners in the last fortnight — if it shows signs of freshness or greenness in the early furlongs it could unsettle runners around it and affect the race shape.
